title: As an American can I purchase a home and live in England?
key_point: Buying UK property gives no visa; mortgage very unlikely for non-resident American; Golden Visas exist elsewhere (Malta).

title: How much cost the live in London for a familly
key_point: French/Swiss engineer budgets GBP70k/yr for family of four; replies estimate GBP3,400-4,000/month core costs.

title: Likelihood of finding Rental Property with Working Fireplace??
key_point: American wants working fireplace; rentals rarely have them due to landlord fire-risk fears and air-quality rules.

title: Coloc mere celibataire
key_point: French single mothers seek house-shares to pool childcare; one pays GBP500/month furnished ensuite studio in Ilford, with pests.

title: Colocations Londres
key_point: French flat-share seekers corrected: post-Brexit work visa needed; budgets under GBP800 for a room.

title: S'installer en famille Londres
key_point: French family: EUR4-6k/month budget tight; bilingual schools ~EUR15k/child; needs airport to CDG within 2h; steered to Bristol.

title: Location meublee a South Kensington
key_point: French mother of three seeks furnished 4-bed South Kensington/Paddington at GBP4-5k/month; feasibility unanswered; visa reminder.

title: Trasferirmi a Londra e scegliere le scuole!
key_point: Italian family: state school places via council after arrival, preferences (Catholic, proximity), waiting lists; placed within a month.

title: Alloggio
key_point: Italian newcomer: single rooms ~GBP520 Eltham, GBP535-560 Plumstead/Woolwich/Norwood/Forest Gate; factor Oyster commute costs.

title: Moving to London (Housing Guidance)
key_point: GBP2,000 1-bed Zone 2 near Elizabeth line; GBP1,850 listing exceeds GBP2,100 with council tax/energy; scams; crime debate.

title: How to rent a house in London before actually arriving in the town?
key_point: Bulgarian couple advised to view in person 2-3 weeks before move; references, month rent plus six weeks deposit.

title: Is credit score an international thing?
key_point: Dutch mover surprised by UK credit scoring; scores do not transfer between countries (US tied to SSN).

title: How much can I negotiate asking price on London rentals?
key_point: Newcomer: London asking rents rarely negotiable; leverage via small landlords, vacancy, quick move-in, days-on-market data.

title: How to open up your first UK bank account without proof of address?
key_point: Address/bank-account catch-22; New-to-UK accounts, opening from home country, work contract; US statements lack sort code.

title: Renting in England without a local credit history
key_point: No UK credit file fails referencing; fix with HR letter, 12-month lease, rent upfront, international credit check.

title: Finding temporary accommodation in London
key_point: Newcomers advised Airbnb/short let first, then search in person; SpareRoom, Rightmove rooms, coliving; scam caution.

title: How do the new 'Right to Rent' checks affect people wanting to rent accommodation in the UK?
key_point: Landlords must check immigration status; penalties GBP80 to GBP3,000; adds steps for foreign renters.

title: Highly Skilled Russian Migrants in London: The Case of IT Professionals (Urban Studies and Practices 2(1):54-63)
key_point: 2000s Russian IT wave settled near City/Canary Wharf or in Chelsea, Hampstead, St John's Wood, Notting Hill, Canada Water; networks used for renting.

title: Immigration and House Prices in the UK (IZA DP 5893; Economic Journal 2015)
key_point: Immigrant inflow of 1% of local population lowers house prices ~1.6% via native out-mobility; driven by low-education migrant areas.

title: Advancing the embedding framework: French highly skilled migrants in London in the context of Brexit (JEMS)
publisher: Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies
key_point: 40 French professionals (2011-2018): children in British schools and British partners anchor staying; Brexit ended their 'invisibility'.

title: The racialization of whiteness in migrants' residential decisions: the case of Polish migrants in England (Ethnic and Racial Studies)
key_point: 41 Polish migrants: neighbourhood safety judged via racial stereotypes; spatial strategies shaped by discrimination. Abstract only.

title: Trading Places: French Highly Skilled Migrants Negotiating Mobility and Emplacement in London (JEMS)
key_point: 37 French finance/business migrants; family considerations shape emplacement in London; 'Eurostars' questioned. Abstract only.

title: Property buyers from US and Canada are fastest growing group
key_point: North Americans 19% of international buyers, Europeans 54%; London international demand +8%; only 5% of NA target PCL; 23% FTB.

title: London's great again! US buyers defy Trump tariff chaos
key_point: US enquiries +~20% YoY; Edinburgh, Westminster, Camden top; 47% seek 1-2 beds; rent if staying under 5 years (stamp duty).

title: Guess who are the 'new oligarchs' buying up London's prime property?
key_point: Californian buyers favour Hampstead/Highgate for greenery; Americans unaffected by non-dom changes as taxed worldwide.

title: US and Gulf buyers drive ultra-prime property market rebound
key_point: US and Gulf buyers 55% of PCL sales above GBP15m in H1 2026; 34 deals, GBP1.24bn, average GBP36.5m.

title: Americans Trump other foreign buyers for London super prime property
key_point: US 6.0% of super-prime buyers, average GBP7.3m; preferred Marylebone, Mayfair, Chelsea, Islington, Belgravia.

title: London remains attractive for international buyers
key_point: Survey of 1,000 in NY, Singapore, Dubai, HK, Paris: 64% would live in London; education 79%, safety 57% valued.

title: Visa holders entering the UK under the Ukraine Humanitarian Schemes
key_point: 45% rent privately; 50% faced barriers renting: 49% no guarantor/references, 42% cannot afford rent.

title: Migrants and Housing in the UK: Experiences and Impacts
key_point: Foreign-born 43% owners vs 67% UK-born; post-2004 EU-born 61% private renters; recent arrivals 17% owners; London overcrowding 14%.

title: Gazumping
key_point: England/Wales offers not binding until exchange (10-12 weeks); Scotland binding via solicitors' letters; US signed agreements bind.

title: Americans in the United Kingdom
key_point: Americans in London mostly business families; Chelsea 6.53% and Kensington 5.81% US-born (2001); 231,853 US-born in UK.

title: Brazilians in the United Kingdom
key_point: Brazilians concentrated in Brent (~30,000), Bayswater ('Brazilwater'), Stockwell; mostly low-wage service jobs.

title: French people in the United Kingdom
key_point: Census 2011: 66,654 French-born in London (48.4%), concentrated in Kensington & Chelsea, Westminster, Hammersmith & Fulham.

title: Lycee Francais Charles de Gaulle
key_point: South Kensington, ~3,500 pupils; annexes Fulham, Ealing, Clapham; fees subsidised for French nationals; community anchor.

title: American School in London
key_point: St John's Wood, ~1,350 pupils, ~80% US passports, ~GBP46k fees; sustains St John's Wood as American family area.

title: Romanians in the United Kingdom
key_point: 175,991 Romanian-born in London (2021); Harrow 21,082; Burnt Oak 'Little Romania'; growth 576% 2011-2021.

title: Poles in the United Kingdom
key_point: Polish clusters Ealing, Hammersmith, Haringey, Hounslow; historic Earl's Court 'Polish Corridor', displaced by costs to Balham/Lewisham.

title: Russians in the United Kingdom
key_point: Russians concentrate in Kensington & Chelsea, Belgravia, Hampstead, Canary Wharf; Russian schools near Notting Hill Gate.
